sentences.en: Heads up, parents.
sentences.zh: 各位家长，请注意。

sentences.en: If you didn't notice it in the title, our topic today is bulls**t jobs.
sentences.zh: 如果你们还没从标题里看出来，我们今天的话题是“狗屁工作”。

sentences.en: That bleep you just heard, it won't be in the rest of the episode.
sentences.zh: 刚才那声消音，在接下来的节目里不会再出现了。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: Many of us at some point in our careers have had jobs that seem pointless.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人在职业生涯的某个阶段，都曾做过看似毫无意义的工作。

sentences.en: I once had a bulls**t job working as a work-study student when I was in college.
sentences.zh: 我上大学时，曾做过一份“狗屁工作”，当时我是个勤工俭学的学生。

sentences.en: I passed out flyers for the streetcar during one summer, and I could not figure out why I was doing that.
sentences.zh: 有一个夏天，我负责为有轨电车发传单，我完全搞不懂自己为什么要干这个。

sentences.en: I've had some temp jobs where I've literally sat in a closet.
sentences.zh: 我还做过一些临时工，真的就是坐在储藏室里。

sentences.en: Jobs where you ask yourself, what am I even doing here?
sentences.zh: 就是那种你会问自己“我到底在这里干什么”的工作。

sentences.en: Like really, what is my actual role at this company?
sentences.zh: 说真的，我在公司里到底扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: If I disappear tomorrow, would anyone notice?
sentences.zh: 如果我明天消失了，会有人注意到吗？

sentences.en: I was doing some paper filing, but they didn't have that much paper filing, and for a week I sat in a supply closet.
sentences.zh: 我当时在做一些文件归档，但其实没那么多文件要归档，有一周的时间，我一直坐在杂物间里。

sentences.en: Doing expense reports and creating like a new piece of paper for every single transaction item on every receipt,
sentences.zh: 处理费用报销单，把每一张收据上的每一笔交易都单独填成一张新表，

sentences.en: for every single thing that expends, like down to like the most minimal thing.
sentences.zh: 每一笔开销都要填，哪怕是再微不足道的小事。

sentences.en: This week we're looking at jobs that feel so pointless, so gut-wrenchingly boring,
sentences.zh: 本周，我们来探讨那些感觉毫无意义、枯燥到让人心碎的工作，

sentences.en: that they are in the words of one expert, bullshit.
sentences.zh: 用一位专家的话说，这些工作就是“狗屁”。

sentences.en: If you don't have one of these jobs yourself, you probably know someone who does.
sentences.zh: 如果你自己没做过这类工作，那你身边肯定也有人做过。

sentences.en: Like the guy binging YouTube videos on his computer at work,
sentences.zh: 比如那个在上班时间疯狂刷 YouTube 视频的家伙，

sentences.en: or the woman who always seems to be playing solitaire.
sentences.zh: 或者那个看起来总是在玩纸牌游戏的女人。

sentences.en: So it was almost all office workers, almost all people who had jobs where, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，这几乎全是办公室职员，几乎都是那些工作状态看起来……你知道的，

sentences.en: you kind of see them there and you kind of wonder, is that guy really doing anything?
sentences.zh: 你看着他们坐在那儿，心里会纳闷：那家伙真的在干活吗？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out, you know, they're not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，他们确实没在干活。

sentences.en: Why do these jobs exist?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些工作会存在？

sentences.en: Why do they seem to be proliferating?
sentences.zh: 为什么它们似乎还在不断增加？

sentences.en: And what effects do these jobs have on us?
sentences.zh: 这些工作对我们有什么影响？

sentences.en: The American TV show The Office tells the story of a paper supply company in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 美国电视剧《办公室》（The Office）讲述了一家宾夕法尼亚州造纸公司的故事。

sentences.en: People show up at work, but it's not always clear what they're doing.
sentences.zh: 人们按时上班，但并不总是清楚自己在做什么。

sentences.en: A lot of the time, people invent pranks or distractions.
sentences.zh: 很多时候，人们会发明一些恶作剧或消遣方式。

sentences.en: You put my stuff in Jell-O again!
sentences.zh: 你又把我的东西放进果冻里了！

sentences.en: They're bored.
sentences.zh: 他们很无聊。

sentences.en: Many of them want to find meaning in their work, but what they're doing is pointless.
sentences.zh: 他们很多人想在工作中寻找意义，但他们所做的事情毫无意义。

sentences.en: You want me to write down people's indefinable qualities?
sentences.zh: 你是要我写下人们那些无法定义的特质吗？

sentences.en: I want you to write down everything that people are doing all day,
sentences.zh: 我是要你写下人们整天都在做的事情，

sentences.en: and then type it up in a way that is helpful.
sentences.zh: 然后整理成有用的文档。

sentences.en: Michael Scott, the boss played by Steve Carell, leads the way.
sentences.zh: 由史蒂夫·卡瑞尔（Steve Carell）饰演的老板迈克尔·斯科特（Michael Scott）带头示范。

sentences.en: I don't want to work.
sentences.zh: 我不想工作。

sentences.en: I just want to bang on this bug all day.
sentences.zh: 我只想整天敲这个虫子。

sentences.en: Did you ask me here for any specific reason?
sentences.zh: 你叫我来是有什么特别的原因吗？

sentences.en: David Graeber has spent quite a bit of time thinking about the many, many real-life versions of Michael Scott.
sentences.zh: 大卫·格雷伯（David Graeber）花了不少时间思考现实生活中迈克尔·斯科特的无数版本。

sentences.en: He's a professor of anthropology at the London School of Economics,
sentences.zh: 他是伦敦政治经济学院的人类学教授，

sentences.en: and he's the author of the book, Bullshit Jobs, A Theory.
sentences.zh: 也是《狗屁工作：一种理论》（Bullshit Jobs, A Theory）一书的作者。

sentences.en: David, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 大卫，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Oh, thank you.
sentences.zh: 哦，谢谢。

sentences.en: So you wrote this essay a couple of years ago that has now turned into a book,
sentences.zh: 你几年前写了这篇文章，现在已经变成了一本书，

sentences.en: and you described an entire category of jobs.
sentences.zh: 你在书中描述了一整类工作。

sentences.en: You call these bullshit jobs, and they're not necessarily menial jobs or boring jobs,
sentences.zh: 你称之为“狗屁工作”，它们不一定是卑微或枯燥的工作，

sentences.en: but they're almost always pointless jobs.
sentences.zh: 但它们几乎总是毫无意义的工作。

sentences.en: Yes, they're actually quite rarely menial.
sentences.zh: 是的，它们实际上很少是卑微的工作。

sentences.en: I mean, there are some cases where people were, say, hired as a museum guard and told to guard a room with nothing in it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些情况下，有人被雇为博物馆保安，被告知去守一个空房间。

sentences.en: That would be both menial and boring.
sentences.zh: 那既卑微又枯燥。

sentences.en: But most often, these jobs are, if nothing else, prestigious and well-paid.
sentences.zh: 但大多数情况下，这些工作至少是体面且高薪的。

sentences.en: A lot of jobs like this are in middle management.
sentences.zh: 很多这类工作都在中层管理岗位。

sentences.en: They're clerical, managerial, administrative sort of positions.
sentences.zh: 它们属于文职、管理、行政之类的职位。

sentences.en: Or their positions in PR, marketing, human resources, almost invariably, they are well-paid, with good benefits,
sentences.zh: 或者是公关、市场、人力资源部门的职位，它们几乎总是高薪且福利优厚，

sentences.en: and you get a lot of prestige, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且你还能获得很高的声望，你知道的。

sentences.en: Yet, at the same time, the people who do them often report themselves genuinely miserable.
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，做这些工作的人往往表示自己真的很痛苦。

sentences.en: You know, they feel they're living a lie.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们觉得自己在过着虚伪的生活。

sentences.en: And not only that, they're living a lie against their will.
sentences.zh: 不仅如此，他们还是违心地过着这种虚伪的生活。

sentences.en: They'd really rather be doing something useful with their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们其实更希望自己的生活能做点有用的事。

sentences.en: So, when you wrote this essay a couple of years ago, I'm not quite sure you anticipated this,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你几年前写这篇文章时，我不确定你是否预料到了这一点，

sentences.en: but the response to the essay was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 但外界对这篇文章的反应非常惊人。

sentences.en: People wrote in from all over the world saying,
sentences.zh: 来自世界各地的人们写信来说：

sentences.en: Help, I'm stuck in a BS job.
sentences.zh: 救救我，我被困在了一份狗屁工作中。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, all over the world, people seem to recognize themselves in the story I told.
sentences.zh: 是的，全世界的人似乎都在我讲述的故事中看到了自己。

sentences.en: And the story I told was almost a joke.
sentences.zh: 而我讲的那个故事几乎像个笑话。

sentences.en: You go to these parties, and you talk to people who are married to academics or, you know, in the business world.
sentences.zh: 你去参加聚会，和那些配偶是学者或者在商界工作的人聊天。

sentences.en: And, well, what do you do?
sentences.zh: 然后问：你做什么工作？

sentences.en: And often it's to say, Oh, nothing, really.
sentences.zh: 通常回答是：哦，没什么，真的。

sentences.en: And, you know, at first they thought they're just being modest or don't think their job is very interesting.
sentences.zh: 起初你以为他们只是谦虚，或者觉得自己的工作没什么意思。

sentences.en: But, you know, apply them of a few drinks, and eventually they will often admit that they meant it literally.
sentences.zh: 但如果你让他们多喝几杯，他们最终往往会承认自己说的是实话。

sentences.en: They literally do nothing.
sentences.zh: 他们确实什么都不做。

sentences.en: So, I wrote this little piece where I basically said, Well, you know, back in the 30s,
sentences.zh: 所以我写了这篇短文，基本上是说，好吧，你知道，在30年代，

sentences.en: they thought we'd be working a 15-hour week by now.
sentences.zh: 人们认为我们现在应该每周只工作15个小时了。

sentences.en: They thought that, you know, mechanization would mean we'd be living lives of leisure.
sentences.zh: 他们认为机械化意味着我们将过上悠闲的生活。

sentences.en: But instead of just, you know, decreasing the working week, what they seem to have done is just made up these imaginary jobs to keep us all busy.
sentences.zh: 但他们似乎并没有缩短工作周，而是编造了这些虚构的工作来让我们都有事可做。

sentences.en: It's almost as if there's, like, some fiendish intelligence making up pointless positions for us to do.
sentences.zh: 就好像有什么邪恶的智慧在为我们编造毫无意义的职位一样。

sentences.en: How did this happen?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: And I wrote this piece, and it just went crazy.
sentences.zh: 我写了这篇文章，然后它就火了。

sentences.en: I really didn't anticipate anything like it.
sentences.zh: 我真的没预料到会这样。

sentences.en: I mean, all over the world, people were translating it, distributing it.
sentences.zh: 全世界的人都在翻译它、传播它。

sentences.en: The server kept crashing.
sentences.zh: 服务器一直崩溃。

sentences.en: Then they put it in newspapers, would run it as a column.
sentences.zh: 后来报纸也把它作为专栏刊登出来。

sentences.en: And you'd get these comment sections, which are just amazing.
sentences.zh: 评论区里的内容简直太精彩了。

sentences.en: People would say things like, Oh, my God, it's true.
sentences.zh: 人们会说：天哪，这是真的。

sentences.en: I'm a corporate lawyer.
sentences.zh: 我是一名企业律师。

sentences.en: I contribute nothing to humanity.
sentences.zh: 我对人类毫无贡献。

sentences.en: I'm just miserable all the time.
sentences.zh: 我一直都很痛苦。

sentences.en: And, you know, confessions started pouring out.
sentences.zh: 各种告白开始涌现。

sentences.en: So I realized this was a much larger phenomenon than I had even imagined.
sentences.zh: 所以我意识到，这比我预想的要大得多。

sentences.en: I understand that polls have been conducted asking people, do you think your job is meaningless?
sentences.zh: 我听说有人做过民意调查，问人们：你觉得你的工作毫无意义吗？

sentences.en: Do you think your job is pointless?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你的工作毫无价值吗？

sentences.en: What do they tell us?
sentences.zh: 他们告诉了我们什么？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, that actually surprised me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，这确实让我感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Because even after the outpouring on the Internet, I thought, okay, you know, maybe 15%, 20% of jobs are like this.
sentences.zh: 因为即使在互联网上引发了热议之后，我还是想，好吧，也许15%到20%的工作是这样的。

sentences.en: And remember, these are people who think their own jobs are pointless.
sentences.zh: 记住，这些人是认为自己的工作毫无意义的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm not going to go and tell somebody who feels his job is meaningful that they're wrong.
sentences.zh: 我不会去告诉一个觉得工作有意义的人说他们错了。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you feel you're not doing anything all day, who would know better than you?
sentences.zh: 但如果你觉得整天什么都没做，谁会比你更清楚呢？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So after a while, they conducted some surveys.
sentences.zh: 所以过了一段时间，他们进行了一些调查。

sentences.en: And one of them was YouGov.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是 YouGov 做的。

sentences.en: And then later, they did another one in Holland.
sentences.zh: 后来，他们在荷兰又做了一次。

sentences.en: And they both came up with pretty much exactly the same results.
sentences.zh: 两者的结果几乎完全一致。

sentences.en: Between 37% to 40% of all people who had jobs were convinced that if their job didn't exist, it would make no difference at all.
sentences.zh: 在所有有工作的人中，有37%到40%的人确信，如果他们的工作不存在，根本不会有任何影响。

sentences.en: That is a huge number, David.
sentences.zh: 这是一个巨大的数字，大卫。

sentences.en: It's insane.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: I had no idea.
sentences.zh: 我完全没想到。

sentences.en: And that's the people who were sure of it.
sentences.zh: 而且这还是那些确定自己工作没意义的人。

sentences.en: You know, only 50% of people were sure their jobs made a difference, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 只有50%的人确信他们的工作确实产生了影响。

sentences.en: And if you think about all the types of jobs there are, no one would possibly doubt that they're fulfilling a useful social function.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想所有的工作类型，没人会怀疑它们在履行有用的社会功能。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I'm sure the number of bus drivers, the number of nurses, the number of mechanics and repairmen, also service workers, actually.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我相信公交司机、护士、机械师和修理工，还有服务人员的数量，确实如此。

sentences.en: You know, I eventually asked people to send in testimonies and stories about their most pointless jobs.
sentences.zh: 我后来请人们发来关于他们最无意义工作的证词和故事。

sentences.en: And almost none of them were in service or retail.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有一个是服务业或零售业的。

sentences.en: It was almost all office workers, almost all people who had jobs where, you know, you kind of see them there and you kind of wonder, is that guy really doing anything?
sentences.zh: 几乎全是办公室职员，几乎都是那些工作状态看起来……你看着他们坐在那儿，心里会纳闷：那家伙真的在干活吗？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out, you know, they're not.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，他们确实没在干活。

sentences.en: You know, David, in your book, you describe the story of Kurt, who is a German military subcontractor.
sentences.zh: 大卫，你在书中描述了库尔特（Kurt）的故事，他是一名德国军事分包商。

sentences.en: And he feels his job is utterly pointless.
sentences.zh: 他觉得自己的工作完全毫无意义。

sentences.en: Why does he feel this way?
sentences.zh: 他为什么会有这种感觉？

sentences.en: Ah, yes, this is one of the first really elaborate examples I got of the kind of job I was talking about, given to me spontaneously by someone on the web.
sentences.zh: 啊，是的，这是我收到的关于我所说的那类工作的第一批非常详尽的例子之一，是网上的人自发告诉我的。

sentences.en: He said, you know, I'm a subcontractor to a subcontractor to a subcontractor, all private firms who work for the German military.
sentences.zh: 他说，我是分包商的分包商的分包商，都是为德国军队工作的私营公司。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, because of outsourcing, if a German soldier wants to move his desktop computer from one office to another, he actually has to fill out a bunch of forMs.
sentences.zh: 他说，因为外包，如果一名德国士兵想把台式电脑从一个办公室搬到另一个办公室，他实际上必须填写一堆表格。

sentences.en: He calls human resources, they call logistics, they call me.
sentences.zh: 他打电话给人力资源部，他们打电话给后勤部，然后他们打电话给我。

sentences.en: Kurt, Sie müssen diesen Computer umstellen, aber schnell.
sentences.zh: “库尔特，你必须把这台电脑搬走，快点。”

sentences.en: And I have to drive 500 kilometers sometimes if I rent a car, drive to wherever this military base is,
sentences.zh: 我有时得开车500公里，如果我租了车，开车去那个军事基地，

sentences.en: fill out a raft of forms, put the thing in a box, it goes down the hall, somebody else takes it out of the box, gives me another form to sign, and then I drive home.
sentences.zh: 填一大堆表格，把东西装进盒子里，它被送到走廊那边，别人把它从盒子里拿出来，给我另一张表格签字，然后我就开车回家。

sentences.en: And that's his entire job.
sentences.zh: 这就是他的全部工作。

sentences.en: And one of the interesting things about these jobs is that people were often very confused about how much people knew and how much they could admit.
sentences.zh: 这些工作有趣的一点是，人们往往非常困惑别人知道多少，以及他们能承认多少。

sentences.en: You know, does my supervisor know that I spend most of the day actually making cat memes?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的主管知道我一天大部分时间其实都在做猫咪表情包吗？

sentences.en: You know, do they know I'm playing computer games?
sentences.zh: 他们知道我在玩电脑游戏吗？

sentences.en: Am I allowed to say, you know, to what degree do my coworkers know?
sentences.zh: 我能说吗？我的同事知道到什么程度？

sentences.en: Can I tell them?
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉他们吗？

sentences.en: You know, there's all these questions that people have.
sentences.zh: 人们有各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: How much do I have to pretend to work?
sentences.zh: 我必须假装工作到什么程度？

sentences.en: And how much am I just allowed to be seen to be just kicking back?
sentences.zh: 我被允许表现出放松的状态到什么程度？

sentences.en: And people are very nervous about this.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到非常紧张。

sentences.en: There are all these gray zones.
sentences.zh: 存在着各种灰色地带。

sentences.en: They'll hire someone, an engineer, in case the air conditioners break.
sentences.zh: 他们会雇佣一个人，一个工程师，以防空调坏了。

sentences.en: For some reason, they find it impossible to just say, well, you're just here in case the air conditioners break.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，他们觉得无法直接说：好吧，你就在这儿待着，以防空调坏了。

sentences.en: Otherwise, try to keep people out of people's way and let them, you know, play cards or, you know, surf the Internet or do whatever they like all day.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，尽量别碍事，让他们整天打牌、上网或者做任何他们喜欢做的事。

sentences.en: Somehow that's not allowed.
sentences.zh: 不知为何，这是不被允许的。

sentences.en: So they have to make up these rituals or at the very least you have to pretend to be working because it's considered somehow insulting not to.
sentences.zh: 所以他们必须编造这些仪式，或者至少你必须假装在工作，因为不这样做被认为是一种侮辱。

sentences.en: And often people really suffered from that, the fact that, A, they had to pretend to some degree.
sentences.zh: 人们往往真的为此感到痛苦，因为他们必须在某种程度上进行伪装。

sentences.en: They couldn't just pursue their own projects.
sentences.zh: 他们不能只追求自己的项目。

sentences.en: And, B, they're never quite sure how much they were allowed to pretend.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们永远不确定自己被允许伪装到什么程度。

sentences.en: This actually leads us to a story that you describe about your own life.
sentences.zh: 这实际上引出了你描述的关于你自己生活的一个故事。

sentences.en: You and some friends signed up to be dishwashers.
sentences.zh: 你和一些朋友报名去当洗碗工。

sentences.en: And something happened on the job.
sentences.zh: 工作中发生了一些事情。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Something happened on the job that made you think about the role of time in how work is constructed.
sentences.zh: 工作中发生的事情让你开始思考时间在工作构建中的作用。

sentences.en: Tell me that story.
sentences.zh: 给我讲讲那个故事。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This is the very first job I had.
sentences.zh: 这是我做的第一份工作。

sentences.en: I think I was 14 years old, maybe 15.
sentences.zh: 我想我当时14岁，也许15岁。

sentences.en: And it was at a beach resort.
sentences.zh: 那是在一个海滨度假村。

sentences.en: And I got a job working as a dishwasher in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 我找了一份在厨房洗碗的工作。

sentences.en: And there was a whole bunch of us who were hired at the same time.
sentences.zh: 当时我们有一大群人同时被录用。

sentences.en: We were all about 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 我们大约都是15岁。

sentences.en: And being 15-year-old boys, you know, when the big rush came, we took it on as a challenge.
sentences.zh: 作为15岁的男孩，你知道，当忙碌的高峰期到来时，我们把它当作一种挑战。

sentences.en: We were like, okay, we are going to be the very best dishwashers of all time.
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，好吧，我们要成为史上最棒的洗碗工。

sentences.en: You know, we're going to be so faSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们要干得飞快。

sentences.en: We're going to be so efficient.
sentences.zh: 我们要非常高效。

sentences.en: The boss is going to be really impressed.
sentences.zh: 老板一定会印象深刻的。

sentences.en: So, you know, we went at it and we, like, finished it in record time and had this huge sparkling pile of dishes and kind of kicked back.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们全力以赴，以创纪录的时间完成了工作，看着那一大堆闪闪发光的盘子，我们便放松了下来。

sentences.en: Boss came in.
sentences.zh: 老板进来了。

sentences.en: We were showing off our handiwork.
sentences.zh: 我们正在炫耀我们的劳动成果。

sentences.en: And he was like, what the hell are you guys just sitting around for?
sentences.zh: 他却说，你们这些家伙坐在这里干什么？

sentences.en: I said, well, we just finished all the dishes.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，我们刚洗完所有的碗。

sentences.en: And he said, yeah, well, keep working.
sentences.zh: 他说，是吗，那就继续干活。

sentences.en: You're on my time.
sentences.zh: 你们是在我的时间里工作。

sentences.en: You're not, you know, you can lounge around on your own time.
sentences.zh: 你们不能，你知道，你们可以在自己的时间里闲逛。

sentences.en: And we were like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 我们当时想，你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I mean, you know, there's nothing to do.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，没什么可做的了。

sentences.en: And he said, well, clean the baseboards.
sentences.zh: 他说，那就去擦踢脚线。

sentences.en: And I said, well, we already cleaned the baseboards.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们已经擦过踢脚线了。

sentences.en: He said, clean them again.
sentences.zh: 他说，再擦一遍。

sentences.en: So we realized that there's this kind of weird idea that there's, like, my time and your time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们意识到，有一种奇怪的观念，即存在“我的时间”和“你的时间”。

sentences.en: If I have paid you money, I own your time.
sentences.zh: 如果我付了钱给你，我就拥有了你的时间。

sentences.en: And you're not allowed to just kick back.
sentences.zh: 你是不允许闲下来的。

sentences.en: You're not allowed to, you know, there's no point in working faSt.
sentences.zh: 你是不允许，你知道，干得快根本没有意义。

sentences.en: That's what we basically learned.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我们学到的东西。

sentences.en: Don't be too efficient because then they'll just make up work.
sentences.zh: 不要太高效，因为那样他们只会编造出更多的工作。

sentences.en: And that experience of doing work that you know isn't necessary just because the boss doesn't want to see you being idle is really degrading.
sentences.zh: 那种明明知道工作没必要，仅仅因为老板不想看到你闲着而去做的工作，真的非常贬低人格。

sentences.en: And it got me to thinking this concept of my time.
sentences.zh: 这让我开始思考“我的时间”这个概念。

sentences.en: How can your time belong to someone else?
sentences.zh: 你的时间怎么可能属于别人呢？

sentences.en: How can you rent time?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能租用时间呢？

sentences.en: And I started doing a little research.
sentences.zh: 我开始做了一些研究。

sentences.en: And I realized, not at the time, but since, that this is a really weird concept that just never would have occurred to most people who've ever lived.
sentences.zh: 我意识到，当时没意识到，但后来明白了，这是一个非常奇怪的概念，对于历史上大多数人来说，这根本是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: You know, in the ancient world, if you see a potter, if you're an ancient Roman or an ancient Greek, you know, you could see a potter and you could imagine buying the pots.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在古代世界，如果你看到一个陶工，如果你是一个古罗马人或古希腊人，你知道，你可以看到一个陶工，你可以想象买他的陶罐。

sentences.en: That's easy, right?
sentences.zh: 这很简单，对吧？

sentences.en: You could imagine buying the potter.
sentences.zh: 你可以想象买下那个陶工。

sentences.en: They had slavery.
sentences.zh: 他们有奴隶制。

sentences.en: But the idea that you could rent this potter's time was just bizarre.
sentences.zh: 但“租用陶工的时间”这个想法简直太离奇了。

sentences.en: It just never would have occurred to anybody.
sentences.zh: 这在任何人脑子里都不会出现。

sentences.en: It takes a whole series of very complicated philosophical and also technological changes that make it possible to take time,
sentences.zh: 这需要一系列非常复杂的哲学和技术变革，才使得把时间拿出来成为可能，

sentences.en: make it into uniform units that can then therefore be bought and sold.
sentences.zh: 把它变成可以买卖的统一单位。

sentences.en: You teach at the London School of Economics.
sentences.zh: 你在伦敦政治经济学院任教。

sentences.en: But before that, you worked at Yale University.
sentences.zh: 但在那之前，你在耶鲁大学工作。

sentences.en: In your book, David, you point out that the cost of education has skyrocketed in many parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 大卫，在你的书中，你指出教育成本在世界许多地方飞涨。

sentences.en: The reason isn't that teachers are being paid more than they were before.
sentences.zh: 原因并不是老师的工资比以前高了。

sentences.en: Instead, you say, universities have gone out and hired an army of workers who are doing BS jobs.
sentences.zh: 相反，你说，大学雇佣了一大批做着废话工作的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is actually really marked in America.
sentences.zh: 是的，这在美国表现得非常明显。

sentences.en: And in America, I have the statistics.
sentences.zh: 在美国，我有统计数据。

sentences.en: The number of administrators has gone up quite sharply, much more so than teachers.
sentences.zh: 行政人员的数量急剧增加，远超教师人数。

sentences.en: But even more important than that, the number of administrative staff has just skyrocketed.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，行政人员的数量简直是呈爆炸式增长。

sentences.en: It's like 240 percent increase over the last 30 years.
sentences.zh: 过去30年里增长了约240%。

sentences.en: So administrative staff basically mean all those guys who work for the deans, for the vice provost, all these endless positions they're constantly making up.
sentences.zh: 所以行政人员基本上是指那些为院长、副教务长工作的人，以及他们不断编造出的各种没完没了的职位。

sentences.en: And what seems to be going on is that these people are being hired essentially for little reason other than making the people now running the universities,
sentences.zh: 看起来发生的情况是，雇佣这些人基本上没什么别的理由，只是为了让现在管理大学的人——

sentences.en: who are no longer the teachers, no longer the professors, but rather top administrators, basically feel good about themselves, feel important.
sentences.zh: 他们不再是老师，不再是教授，而是高级行政人员——感到自我良好，感到自己很重要。

sentences.en: They hire these guys who are basically there, almost like feudal retainers.
sentences.zh: 他们雇佣这些人，这些人基本上就像封建时代的家臣。

sentences.en: You know, I get hired as a vice provoSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我被聘为副教务长。

sentences.en: So obviously I need four or five assistants.
sentences.zh: 所以显然我需要四五个助理。

sentences.en: You know, they decide what the assistants will actually do later.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们以后再决定助理具体做什么。

sentences.en: Assistant's trying to figure out something to do.
sentences.zh: 助理在努力想办法找点事做。

sentences.en: So the assistant says, I know, I'll fill out, you know, I'll do a time allocation study.
sentences.zh: 于是助理说，我知道了，我会填一份，你知道，我会做一个时间分配研究。

sentences.en: And then suddenly people like me have to spend like hours every week filling out time allocation studies, breaking down exactly what I do at every hour of the day.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，像我这样的人每周都要花几个小时填写时间分配研究，详细分解我每天每小时都在做什么。

sentences.en: So I can't actually do stuff because I'm filling out the forMs.
sentences.zh: 所以我根本没法做正事，因为我一直在填表。

sentences.en: And this is how it works.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样运作的。

sentences.en: Like the more of these guys there are in these bullshit jobs, the less time the people with real jobs have to actually do their work.
sentences.zh: 这些做着废话工作的人越多，真正有工作要做的人能用来做正事的时间就越少。

sentences.en: And this isn't just universities.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅发生在大学里。

sentences.en: I mean, the same thing's happening in hospitals.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，医院里也发生了同样的事情。

sentences.en: More and more hospital administrators means nurses have to spend more and more time doing paperwork and less time nursing.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的医院行政人员意味着护士必须花越来越多的时间处理文书工作，而花在护理上的时间却减少了。

sentences.en: Primary schools, same thing.
sentences.zh: 小学也是一样。

sentences.en: Teachers just have to spend all their time in meetings and reports.
sentences.zh: 老师们不得不把所有时间都花在开会和写报告上。

sentences.en: Okay, by this point you might be looking around at fellow commuters, at co-workers, at friends, and asking yourself,
sentences.zh: 好吧，说到这里，你可能会环顾四周的通勤者、同事、朋友，问自己：

sentences.en: which people find their work boring and pointless?
sentences.zh: 哪些人觉得自己的工作枯燥且毫无意义？

sentences.en: It turns out there are tells to identify people doing bullshit jobs.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，有一些迹象可以识别出那些做着废话工作的人。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收看。

sentences.en: Working a bullshit job might feel like an exercise in futility, a task that seems completely pointless.
sentences.zh: 做一份废话工作可能感觉就像是在做无用功，一项看起来完全毫无意义的任务。

sentences.en: In truth, there's a perverse logic that shapes how and why these jobs come to be.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这些工作之所以出现，背后有一种扭曲的逻辑。

sentences.en: David Graeber has brought an anthropologist's eye to the life of the bored office worker,
sentences.zh: 大卫·格雷伯以人类学家的视角审视了枯燥的上班族生活，

sentences.en: and he's come up with a classification system for different kinds of BS jobs.
sentences.zh: 并为不同类型的废话工作建立了一套分类系统。

sentences.en: The first category is something he calls a duct taper.
sentences.zh: 第一类他称之为“打补丁者”。

sentences.en: Rather than fix serious headaches, many organizations take the easy route.
sentences.zh: 许多组织不是去解决严重的难题，而是选择走捷径。

sentences.en: They paper over the problem.
sentences.zh: 他们只是掩盖问题。

sentences.en: David has a revealing story from his own life.
sentences.zh: 大卫有一个来自他亲身经历的揭示性故事。

sentences.en: This was quite early on in my time in the U.K.
sentences.zh: 那是我刚到英国大学系统工作时，办公室里有一个架子。

sentences.en: university system, and they had this shelf in my office.
sentences.zh: 我一直有点担心它。

sentences.en: I was always a little worried about it.
sentences.zh: 它看起来摇摇欲坠。

sentences.en: It seemed kind of precarious.
sentences.zh: 有一天，它完全从墙上脱落了。

sentences.en: And one day it just completely ripped out of the wall.
sentences.zh: 墙上出现了一个巨大的洞。

sentences.en: There was this huge gaping hole in the wall.
sentences.zh: 扭曲的金属挂在我的桌子上。

sentences.en: There was this mangled metal, you know, hanging over my desk.
sentences.zh: 显然我不可能自己修好它。

sentences.en: There's obviously no way I could fix it myself.
sentences.zh: 所以我给基建部门打了电话，他们说，好的，我们会派个木匠来。

sentences.en: And so I called, you know, buildings and grounds, and, you know, they said, okay, we'll send a carpenter.
sentences.zh: 木匠花了一个半星期才出现。

sentences.en: And it took about a week and a half for the carpenter to show up.
sentences.zh: 办公室里的人都在打电话。

sentences.en: And people in the office were calling.
sentences.zh: 我也在打。

sentences.en: I was calling.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在打。

sentences.en: Everybody was calling.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种日常仪式。

sentences.en: And it became this daily ritual.
sentences.zh: 我逐渐意识到有一个人，我们总是找同一个人，

sentences.en: And I gradually realized there's one guy, we always got the same guy,
sentences.zh: 他的全部工作似乎就是为木匠太忙没法过来而道歉。

sentences.en: whose entire job seemed to consist of apologizing for the fact that the carpenter was very busy and couldn't come.
sentences.zh: 有一天我突然想到，为什么他们不直接解雇那个人，再雇一个木匠呢？

sentences.en: And one day it occurred to me, like, well, why don't they just fire that guy and hire a second carpenter?
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为那样他们就不需要他了，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, because then they won't need him, right?
sentences.zh: 我向不同的人提到了这一点，他们看着我，好像在说，是啊，那怎么可能发生。

sentences.en: And I mentioned this to various people, and they looked at me like, yeah, right, that would ever happen.
sentences.zh: 我意识到这是一个废话工作的完美例子。

sentences.en: And I realized that this is a perfect example of a bullshit job.
sentences.zh: 他的工作之所以必要，仅仅是因为这个系统构建得太愚蠢了。

sentences.en: His job is only necessitated because the system is stupidly constructed.
sentences.zh: 所以他待在那里，你知道，这相当于如果你的屋顶漏水，你不去修屋顶，而是雇一个人每小时倒一次水桶。

sentences.en: So he's there to, you know, it's the equivalent of if you had a leak in the roof, instead of fixing the roof, you hire some guy to empty a bucket every hour.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个完全毫无意义的职位。

sentences.en: You know, it's a totally pointless position.
sentences.zh: 我逐渐意识到，至少在软件行业，这被称为“打补丁”。

sentences.en: And gradually I realized that in the software industry, at least, this is called duct taping.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想谈谈第二类废话工作。

sentences.en: I want to talk about a second category of bullshit jobs, David.
sentences.zh: 这一类涉及那些为下属想出毫无意义的任务的经理。

sentences.en: This one involves managers who come up with meaningless assignments for their subordinates.
sentences.zh: 你称他们为“监工”？

sentences.en: You call them taskmasters?
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 监工是一种废话工作，涉及，嗯，实际上有两种不同的类型。

sentences.en: Now, a taskmaster is a type of bullshit job which involves, well, there's two different types, actually.
sentences.zh: 其中一种仅仅是监督那些根本不需要监督的人。

sentences.en: One of them is simply a supervisor of people who don't need supervision.
sentences.zh: 很多中层管理人员写信给我说他们就是那种工作。

sentences.en: And a lot of middle managers wrote to me and said that they had that kind of job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，通常他们做过某项工作，被提升到管理层，所以他们知道做这项工作需要什么。

sentences.en: You know, often they'd done a certain job, they got promoted to management, so they knew what was entailed doing the job.
sentences.zh: 他们知道下属根本不需要监督，但他们还是得假装在监督他们。

sentences.en: And they knew that basically they didn't need supervision at all, but they had to pretend they were supervising them anyway.
sentences.zh: 但另一种类型正是我在大学案例中描述的那种，

sentences.en: But another type is exactly what I was describing in the case of universities,
sentences.zh: 那些工作最终似乎变成了为别人制造文书工作和不必要任务的人。

sentences.en: people whose job seems to end up being creating paperwork and unnecessary tasks for other people to do.
sentences.zh: 所以，回到中层管理的例子，假设你做过一份工作，然后被提升去监督那份工作，你知道他们不需要监督。

sentences.en: So, again, to go back to the middle management example, say you did have a job and you got promoted to supervising that job and you knew that they didn't need supervision.
sentences.zh: 渐渐地，你会意识到，与其整天坐在这里，为了在老板面前表现得好，最好的办法可能就是建立某种目标系统。

sentences.en: Gradually, you would realize that rather than just sit here all day, probably the best thing you could do to look good to your boss is to create some kind of target system.
sentences.zh: 你知道，给他们布置文书工作，确保他们达到目标，然后就会有东西需要归档和处理，你也就有事可做了。

sentences.en: You know, give them paperwork to do to make sure they're hitting their targets, and then there'll be something to file and process, and you'll have something that you can do.
sentences.zh: 经典的例子来自一个叫克洛伊的女性的故事。

sentences.en: The classic example comes from the story of a woman named Chloe.
sentences.zh: 她是少数几个愿意站出来向我承认这一点的学术管理高层之一。

sentences.en: She was one of the few people who was in academic administration in the higher echelons who was willing to come forward and admit this to me.
sentences.zh: 她说，嗯，你知道，我接受了这份非执行院长的职位。

sentences.en: She said, well, you know, I took on this job as a non-executive dean.
sentences.zh: 她说，非执行基本上意味着你没有权力，不控制资金，所以你是战略性的。

sentences.en: She says, non-executive basically means you have no power, you don't control money, so you're strategic.
sentences.zh: 你应该提出想法，但你没有真正的能力让任何人去执行。

sentences.en: You're supposed to come up with ideas, but you have no real ability to make anybody do that.
sentences.zh: 所以本质上，她有一份毫无意义的工作。

sentences.en: So essentially, she had a pointless job.
sentences.zh: 她会提出一个计划，然后没人会理会。

sentences.en: She would come up with a plan, and then nobody would pay any attention.
sentences.zh: 然而，她被分配了三个助理。

sentences.en: However, she was given three assistants.
sentences.zh: 同样，这就是会发生的事情。

sentences.en: Again, that's what happens.
sentences.zh: 一旦你得到了一个显赫的职位，他们立刻就会给你分配助理，然后你必须想办法给他们找点事做。

sentences.en: As soon as you get a prestigious position, they immediately give you assistants, and then you have to figure out something for them to do.
sentences.zh: 在她的案例中，他们都没有任何明显的功能，所以她不得不花时间编造一些事情让他们做，以免他们因为闲着而惹麻烦。

sentences.en: In her case, none of them had any obvious function, so she had to spend her time making up things for them to do so they wouldn't get in trouble for just sitting around.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以有废话工作来帮助老板感觉自己是必要的，尽管他其实并不必要。

sentences.en: So you can have BS jobs to help the boss feel like he's actually necessary when he isn't.
sentences.zh: 你可以有旨在掩盖组织无法或不想解决的问题的废话工作。

sentences.en: You can have BS jobs that are designed to paper over problems that an organization cannot or does not want to fix.
sentences.zh: 大卫还描述了第三种废话工作。

sentences.en: David also describes a third type of BS job.
sentences.zh: 从表面上看，这些工作并非毫无意义，但组织拥有它们的唯一原因是因为其他组织也有这些工作。

sentences.en: On the surface, these jobs are not pointless, but the only reason an organization has them is because other organizations have them.
sentences.zh: 大卫称这些工作的人为“打手”。

sentences.en: David calls the people who work these jobs goons.
sentences.zh: 我问他这个词是什么意思。

sentences.en: I asked him what he meant by the term.
sentences.zh: 我不得不编造这个词，因为太多人写信给我，说他们做着我没预料到的工作，这些工作涉及某种侵略性，

sentences.en: I had to make that up because so many people wrote to me with jobs that I hadn't really anticipated, jobs which involved a certain element of aggression,
sentences.zh: 这在公司看来可能是必要或有帮助的。

sentences.en: which might have seemed necessary or helpful to the corporation.
sentences.zh: 它们并非完全没用，但做这些工作的人觉得它们本不该存在，

sentences.en: They weren't completely useless, but that the people doing them felt shouldn't exist anyway,
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是因为他们觉得整个行业或职业都是不必要的。

sentences.en: largely because they felt the entire industry or profession was unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 所以电话推销员就是一个很好的例子。

sentences.en: So telemarketers were a great example.
sentences.zh: 电话推销员强烈地认为，我的意思是，我相信95%的电话推销员，

sentences.en: Telemarketers felt strongly that, I mean, 95 percent of telemarketers, I'm sure,
sentences.zh: 都强烈地认为如果所有的电话推销员都凭空消失，世界会变得更美好。

sentences.en: feel strongly that if all telemarketers were to vanish in a puff of smoke, the world would be a better place.
sentences.zh: 但很多企业律师也有这种感觉。

sentences.en: But a lot of corporate lawyers feel that way, too.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，当然，有一些高层会争辩说企业法非常重要。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, sure, there's some higher ups who would argue no corporate law is very important.
sentences.zh: 它把一切维系在一起。

sentences.en: It holds things together.
sentences.zh: 它把一切维系在一起。

sentences.en: But, you know, most corporate lawyers I've talked to, usually the lower ranking ones, will say, oh, come on.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我接触过的大多数企业律师，通常是级别较低的那些，都会说，噢，算了吧。

sentences.en: I mean, if this entire industry were to disappear, it would be great.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果整个行业消失了，那才好呢。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, you only need a corporate lawyer, but somebody else has a corporate lawyer.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，你只需要一个企业律师，但别人也有企业律师。

sentences.en: It's a little like a feudal lord.
sentences.zh: 这有点像封建领主。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, they always say feudal lords are there to protect the peasants, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，他们总是说封建领主是为了保护农民而存在的，对吧？

sentences.en: That's their justification for taking feudal rents.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们收取封建地租的理由。

sentences.en: But, you know, if you really look into the matter, who are they protecting the peasants from?
sentences.zh: 但你知道，如果你深入研究这个问题，他们是在保护农民免受谁的伤害呢？

sentences.en: Other feudal lords.
sentences.zh: 其他封建领主。

sentences.en: So, you know, if there were no feudal lords, feudal lords would be unnecessary.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果没有封建领主，封建领主也就没必要存在了。

sentences.en: So that's why I call them goons.
sentences.zh: 所以我称他们为打手。

sentences.en: There's an element of aggression there.
sentences.zh: 这其中有一种侵略性的成分。

sentences.en: But on the other hand, you know, they're only there because other such aggressive people exiSt.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面，你知道，他们之所以存在，仅仅是因为其他同样具有侵略性的人存在。

sentences.en: David says another BS job is the flunky.
sentences.zh: 大卫说另一种狗屁工作是跟班。

sentences.en: These jobs primarily exist to make someone or something look impressive.
sentences.zh: 这些工作的存在主要是为了让某人或某事看起来令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: Classic flunkies of the past have included things like doormen or footmen.
sentences.zh: 过去典型的跟班包括门房或男仆之类的角色。

sentences.en: You know, I always wonder what a footman actually was.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我一直很好奇男仆到底是做什么的。

sentences.en: You always read about them in Alice in Wonderland in these 19th century books.
sentences.zh: 你在《爱丽丝梦游仙境》这些19世纪的书里总能读到他们。

sentences.en: You know what a footman was?
sentences.zh: 你知道男仆是做什么的吗？

sentences.en: They were the guys who wore these really, you know, fancy military looking uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 他们就是那些穿着非常、你知道，花哨的军装风格制服的人。

sentences.en: But the thing they actually did was they ran in front of people's carriages looking for bumps in the road.
sentences.zh: 但他们实际做的事情是跑在人们的马车前面，寻找路上的坑洼。

sentences.en: So, you know, the whole idea is if I have a servant just to do this one basically kind of superfluous, not really totally necessary thing, I'm really rich and important.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，整个想法就是如果我雇一个仆人专门做这种基本上多余、并非完全必要的事情，我就显得非常富有和重要。

sentences.en: So you should know that.
sentences.zh: 所以你应该知道这一点。

sentences.en: And that's a classic flunky.
sentences.zh: 那是一个典型的跟班。

sentences.en: Often flunkies will be assigned one very minor task, sort of like the guy who tweezers the Lord's mustache before a joust or something like that.
sentences.zh: 跟班通常会被分配一项非常微小的任务，有点像在比武前给领主的胡子夹毛的人之类的。

sentences.en: But really, they're just there so that everybody can know I've got lots of servants.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，他们只是为了让每个人都知道我有很多仆人。

sentences.en: But in the corporate world, it's very much the same because in the corporate world, the actual status of an executive is often measured by how many people work under.
sentences.zh: 但在企业界，情况非常相似，因为在企业界，高管的实际地位通常是通过他手下有多少人来衡量的。

sentences.en: So he has no incentive to get rid of unnecessary employees.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有动力去裁掉不必要的员工。

sentences.en: And, in fact, you often find people saying, yeah, I'm just there to make someone else look important or seem important.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你经常会听到人们说，是的，我只是为了让别人看起来重要或显得重要。

sentences.en: Receptionists often say that.
sentences.zh: 前台接待员经常这么说。

sentences.en: You know, obviously, some receptionists are very busy and have a real job.
sentences.zh: 你知道，显然，有些接待员非常忙，有真正的工作要做。

sentences.en: But there are some receptionists who, you know, maybe they get one phone call a day, too.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些接待员，你知道，可能一天只接一个电话。

sentences.en: Otherwise, they change the candy bowl or, you know, water the plants or something.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，他们就是换换糖果碗，或者，你知道，给植物浇水之类的。

sentences.en: But basically, they're just sitting around.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，他们只是坐在那里。

sentences.en: So why do they have a receptionist at all?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么他们还要雇佣接待员呢？

sentences.en: You know, if it's just one call a day, they could just take the call themselves, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果一天只有一个电话，他们完全可以自己接，对吧？

sentences.en: The reason why is because if you don't have a receptionist, you don't look like a real corporation.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，如果你没有接待员，你看起来就不像一家真正的公司。

sentences.en: One reason that companies end up with BS jobs is that it's sometimes difficult or impossible or unpleasant to get rid of people who are not functioning well.
sentences.zh: 公司最终出现狗屁工作的一个原因是，有时要解雇那些表现不佳的人是很困难、不可能或令人不快的。

sentences.en: You mentioned the example of the guy who's apologizing for the carpenter not showing up.
sentences.zh: 你提到了那个为木匠没出现而道歉的人的例子。

sentences.en: Now, it could just be that getting rid of that guy and hiring another carpenter might be administratively onerous.
sentences.zh: 现在，可能仅仅是因为解雇那个人并雇佣另一个木匠在行政上很麻烦。

sentences.en: So talk to me about this idea that part of the problem might actually just be, you know, rigidity in how organizations work.
sentences.zh: 所以跟我谈谈这个想法，即问题的一部分可能实际上只是，你知道，组织运作方式的僵化。

sentences.en: And instead of basically, you know, getting rid of the person you don't want and finding the person you do want,
sentences.zh: 而不是基本上，你知道，摆脱你不想要的人并找到你想要的人，

sentences.en: you end up sometimes just keeping the person you don't want or now hiring an additional person to come in and do the job that you actually do need to get done.
sentences.zh: 你有时最终只是留下了你不想要的人，或者现在又雇了一个额外的人进来做你真正需要完成的工作。

sentences.en: That was one of my favorite examples, actually, because, you know,
sentences.zh: 那实际上是我最喜欢的例子之一，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: the taskmasters are obviously the ones where it's most difficult to get them to fess up and send in testimonies about what's going on.
sentences.zh: 监工显然是最难让他们坦白并提交关于正在发生什么的情况说明的人。

sentences.en: But I got a couple and one of them said exactly that one reason that you end up getting so many bullshit jobs in large bureaucracies is if someone has seniority and, you know,
sentences.zh: 但我确实得到了一些，其中一个说得完全正确，在大规模官僚机构中，你最终会得到这么多狗屁工作的一个原因是，如果某人有资历，而且，你知道，

sentences.en: good reports, well, it's almost impossible to fire them.
sentences.zh: 报告良好，嗯，几乎不可能解雇他们。

sentences.en: So if suddenly they become a drunk or just, you know, lose interest in the job, become bad at what they do,
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们突然变成了酒鬼，或者只是，你知道，对工作失去了兴趣，变得不称职，

sentences.en: the easiest thing to do instead of getting rid of them is to hire someone else to do their job.
sentences.zh: 最简单的做法不是解雇他们，而是雇佣别人来做他们的工作。

sentences.en: But if you hire someone else to do their job, you can't admit that they're doing their job, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果你雇佣别人来做他们的工作，你不能承认他们在做他们的工作，对吧？

sentences.en: So you have to make up a different job.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须编造一份不同的工作。

sentences.en: And then often you have to walk them through, get them, you know, tell them what to put on their CV so they look like they can do this other thing,
sentences.zh: 然后你通常还得指导他们，让他们，你知道，告诉他们在简历上写什么，这样他们看起来就能做这件别的事情，

sentences.en: even though really they're going to be doing, you know, what the drunk guy does.
sentences.zh: 尽管实际上他们要做的是，你知道，那个酒鬼做的事情。

sentences.en: And so you have these elaborate rituals of creating dummy jobs.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有这些创造虚假工作的复杂仪式。

sentences.en: And then, you know, when that guy goes, you might need to hire someone to actually do the made up job.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，当那个人走了，你可能需要雇人来真正做那份编造的工作。

sentences.en: And it just becomes endlessly Machiavellian and elaborate.
sentences.zh: 这变得没完没了地阴险和复杂。

sentences.en: What we're doing here, Michael handles more of the big picture stuff and I handle more of the day-to-day stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里做的是，迈克尔处理更多大局方面的事情，我处理更多日常琐事。

sentences.en: So together...
sentences.zh: 所以在一起……

sentences.en: I think I understand.
sentences.zh: 我想我明白了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Each of you is doing half a job.
sentences.zh: 你们每个人都在做半份工作。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Sometimes I can hardly handle that.
sentences.zh: 有时我几乎无法应付。

sentences.en: When we come back, the psychological consequences of working in a job that you not only find boring, but that you think is meaningless.
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，将讨论从事一份你不仅觉得无聊，而且认为毫无意义的工作所带来的心理后果。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the range of psychological effects that you describe that arise from doing these kinds of BS jobs.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈你所描述的由从事这类狗屁工作而产生的各种心理影响。

sentences.en: And I want to begin with research that you cite that was done amongst babies that you say sort of shows the value of meaningful work.
sentences.zh: 我想从你引用的关于婴儿的研究开始，你说这在某种程度上展示了有意义工作的价值。

sentences.en: What was the research?
sentences.zh: 那项研究是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was really interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: I'd heard this expression and it always stuck in my head, the pleasure at being a cause.
sentences.zh: 我听说过这个表达，它一直印在我的脑海里，即“作为原因的快乐”。

sentences.en: It always made sense to me somehow, you know?
sentences.zh: 它不知何故总是让我觉得很有道理，你知道吗？

sentences.en: A lot of what we do, which seems fun, doesn't seem to have any point, but it's just like knowing that you can do things itself is kind of fun.
sentences.zh: 我们做的很多事情，看起来很有趣，似乎没有任何意义，但仅仅是知道你能做某事本身就很有趣。

sentences.en: And indeed, there was a German psychologist who was trying to come up with a theory of play, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，确实有一位德国心理学家试图提出一个关于游戏的理论。

sentences.en: And he noticed something very interesting.
sentences.zh: 他注意到了一些非常有趣的事情。

sentences.en: He noticed that infants, when they're first trying to figure out who they are, because, you know,
sentences.zh: 他注意到婴儿，当他们第一次试图弄清楚自己是谁时，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: at first infants don't even really understand that they are a discrete entity separate from the world around them.
sentences.zh: 起初婴儿甚至不真正理解他们是一个独立于周围世界的个体。

sentences.en: Where they stop and the world starts is not clear to them, you know?
sentences.zh: 他们在哪里结束，世界在哪里开始，这对他们来说并不清楚，你知道吗？

sentences.en: They're kind of continuous with their mother.
sentences.zh: 他们和母亲在某种程度上是连续的。

sentences.en: They're continuous with their environment.
sentences.zh: 他们和环境是连续的。

sentences.en: Okay, so babies actually figure out that they are a discrete entity.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以婴儿实际上弄清楚了他们是一个独立的个体。

sentences.en: At the moment, they realize they can have predictable effects on the world.
sentences.zh: 就在他们意识到自己可以对世界产生可预测的影响的那一刻。

sentences.en: So there's some point where a child, say, they're moving their arm around and they move something on the table, you know, like move a pencil.
sentences.zh: 所以有那么一点，孩子，比如说，他们挥动手臂，移动了桌子上的东西，你知道，比如移动一支铅笔。

sentences.en: And they realize if they move their arm the same way, the pencil will move in the same way as well.
sentences.zh: 他们意识到如果他们以同样的方式移动手臂，铅笔也会以同样的方式移动。

sentences.en: And the moment where they realize that, there's this sort of feeling of incredible happiness comes over a child.
sentences.zh: 就在他们意识到那一刻，孩子会产生一种难以置信的幸福感。

sentences.en: You can see them just, like, absolute joy and delight.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到他们，就像，绝对的快乐和喜悦。

sentences.en: Like, wow, I can move a pencil.
sentences.zh: 就像，哇，我可以移动一支铅笔。

sentences.en: This is great.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: It'll happen the same way every time.
sentences.zh: 它每次都会以同样的方式发生。

sentences.en: And that moment, they say, is the moment you realize that you are something different from the world.
sentences.zh: 他们说，那一刻就是你意识到你与世界不同的时刻。

sentences.en: You know, you are a thing that can have effects on the world.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你是一个可以对世界产生影响的东西。

sentences.en: And what they argue is that sense of self is tied up with that kind of joyous realization that you can have effects on the world.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，自我意识与那种你可以对世界产生影响的快乐实现紧密相连。

sentences.en: What happens when small children are prevented from influencing their worlds?
sentences.zh: 当幼儿被阻止影响他们的世界时会发生什么？

sentences.en: David says they experience a decline in well-being and efficacy.
sentences.zh: 大卫说他们会经历幸福感和效能感的下降。

sentences.en: Kids freak out.
sentences.zh: 孩子们会抓狂。

sentences.en: You know, they go from being incredibly happy to being really confused and upset.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们从极其快乐变得非常困惑和不安。

sentences.en: You're blocked from having any meaningful effect on the world around you.
sentences.zh: 你被阻止对周围世界产生任何有意义的影响。

sentences.en: You kind of collapse.
sentences.zh: 你会有点崩溃。

sentences.en: Now, I really think that's what's happening in the case of bullshit jobs.
sentences.zh: 现在，我真的认为这就是狗屁工作所发生的情况。

sentences.en: People suddenly become incredibly depressed.
sentences.zh: 人们突然变得极其沮丧。

sentences.en: They lose all motivation.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了所有的动力。

sentences.en: They don't understand why they feel that way.
sentences.zh: 他们不明白为什么会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: That's, you know, in a way, they think, I should be happy, right?
sentences.zh: 那是，你知道，在某种程度上，他们想，我应该很高兴，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm getting paid money to do nothing, something for nothing.
sentences.zh: 我拿着钱什么都不做，不劳而获。

sentences.en: That's a great deal.
sentences.zh: 那是一笔很划算的交易。

sentences.en: But why am I so miserable?
sentences.zh: 但我为什么这么痛苦？

sentences.en: I think that's the reason.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是原因。

sentences.en: I remember once talking with Peter Ubel.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次和彼得·乌贝尔交谈。

sentences.en: He's a researcher at Duke University.
sentences.zh: 他是杜克大学的研究员。

sentences.en: He once conducted a study.
sentences.zh: 他曾经进行过一项研究。

sentences.en: He told volunteers that they could sit silently, you know, no iPhones, no distractions, nothing, for five minutes.
sentences.zh: 他告诉志愿者，他们可以静静地坐着，你知道，没有iPhone，没有干扰，什么都没有，坐五分钟。

sentences.en: And if they did that, they would get $2.50.
sentences.zh: 如果他们那样做了，他们会得到2.5美元。

sentences.en: He also told them that they could spend the time solving very, very difficult probleMs.
sentences.zh: 他还告诉他们，他们可以花时间解决非常、非常困难的问题。

sentences.en: And he asked them how much would they want to be paid for doing the puzzles instead of doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 他问他们，比起什么都不做，他们想要多少报酬来做这些谜题。

sentences.en: Here's what Ubel told me.
sentences.zh: 这是乌贝尔告诉我的。

sentences.en: We found that the large majority of the students said we'd have to pay them more than $2.50 to solve the word puzzles.
sentences.zh: 我们发现绝大多数学生说我们必须支付他们超过2.5美元才能解决这些字谜。

sentences.en: And yet when we actually finished the five minutes and asked them how much they enjoyed those five minutes,
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们真正结束了五分钟并问他们有多享受那五分钟时，

sentences.en: the people solving the word puzzles enjoyed the five minutes significantly more.
sentences.zh: 那些解决字谜的人明显更享受那五分钟。

sentences.en: And yet very few of them said, yeah, pay me $2 and I'd be happy to do word puzzles because at least I'll be having fun.
sentences.zh: 然而很少有人说，是的，付我2美元，我很乐意做字谜，因为至少我会玩得很开心。

sentences.en: One implication from the study, David, is that people don't fully appreciate all the dimensions of a job when they apply for it.
sentences.zh: 大卫，这项研究的一个启示是，人们在申请工作时并没有完全理解工作的各个维度。

sentences.en: So you might think, hey, it's great to get paid money for doing absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会想，嘿，什么都不做就能拿到钱真是太好了。

sentences.en: But the issue of boredom, the issue of meaninglessness, the issue of pointlessness,
sentences.zh: 但无聊的问题、无意义的问题、毫无价值的问题，

sentences.en: these things become salient only after you've started doing the job.
sentences.zh: 这些问题只有在你开始工作后才会变得突出。

sentences.en: So in some ways, are psychological biases partly to blame for the proliferation of BS jobs?
sentences.zh: 那么在某种程度上，心理偏见是否是狗屁工作泛滥的部分原因？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's partly, too, that we're all taught that people want something for nothing.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为部分原因也是，我们都被教导人们想要不劳而获。

sentences.en: I mean, think about economics.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想经济学。

sentences.en: What does economics teach you?
sentences.zh: 经济学教给你什么？

sentences.en: Basically that we all want something for nothing, that, you know,
sentences.zh: 基本上我们都想要不劳而获，你知道，

sentences.en: people wish to get the maximum benefit for the least expenditure of time and resources and effort.
sentences.zh: 人们希望以最少的时间、资源和努力支出获得最大的利益。

sentences.en: So, you know, according to economics, anybody who's handed a job where they're paid good money to do nothing should be happy as a clam, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，根据经济学，任何被分配到一份拿着高薪却什么都不做的工作的人都应该像蛤蜊一样快乐，你知道。

sentences.en: But so one of the strange things is that people don't understand why they aren't happy.
sentences.zh: 但奇怪的事情之一是，人们不明白为什么他们不快乐。

sentences.en: We're given this false assumption about what people are basically about and what people are basically like.
sentences.zh: 我们被灌输了关于人们本质上是什么以及人们本质上像什么的错误假设。

sentences.en: You argue that there are even spiritual consequences of BS jobs, and one of them is something that you call scriptlessness.
sentences.zh: 你认为狗屁工作甚至有精神层面的后果，其中之一就是你所说的“无剧本状态”。

sentences.en: What do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I remember being very impressed by a psychological study which looked at people, you know,
sentences.zh: 我记得对一项心理学研究印象非常深刻，它观察人们，你知道，

sentences.en: sort of looked at times they'd been in love or people had been in love with them when they were teenagers and how they'd managed to integrate the experience,
sentences.zh: 观察他们青少年时期恋爱或被爱的时光，以及他们如何设法整合这种经历，

sentences.en: especially unrequited love.
sentences.zh: 尤其是单相思。

sentences.en: And what they found out was that, you know, if you're in love with someone who does not return your feelings, well, you know, it's difficult,
sentences.zh: 他们发现的是，你知道，如果你爱上了一个没有回应你感情的人，嗯，你知道，这很困难，

sentences.en: but you can come up with a story about it.
sentences.zh: 但你可以编出一个关于它的故事。

sentences.en: You know, people had come to terms with it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们已经接受了它。

sentences.en: They almost remembered the incidents fondly 20 years later.
sentences.zh: 20年后，他们几乎还能怀念地想起这些事件。

sentences.en: It was the people who had other people who were in love with them who didn't actually feel the same way about them who were still kind of hurting.
sentences.zh: 是那些有别人爱着他们，但他们实际上对对方没有同样感觉的人，仍然感到有点受伤。

sentences.en: They were really confused.
sentences.zh: 他们真的很困惑。

sentences.en: They felt guilty, but they felt indignant.
sentences.zh: 他们感到内疚，但他们感到愤慨。

sentences.en: They just didn't know how to feel.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不知道该有什么感觉。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons why they suggested is because, you know, if you're in love with someone who doesn't love you, you know exactly how you're supposed to feel.
sentences.zh: 他们建议的原因之一是，你知道，如果你爱上了一个不爱你的人，你知道你该有什么感觉。

sentences.en: There's like 2,000 years of literature telling you exactly how you're supposed to feel, how you're supposed to behave, what's appropriate, what isn't.
sentences.zh: 有两千年的文学作品告诉你到底该有什么感觉，该如何表现，什么是合适的，什么是不合适的。

sentences.en: Whereas if you're on the other side, you're pretty much at a loss.
sentences.zh: 而如果你在另一边，你基本上不知所措。

sentences.en: You know, there are no novels written from the point of view of Roxanne instead of, you know, Cyrano.
sentences.zh: 你知道，没有小说是从罗克珊的角度而不是，你知道，西拉诺的角度写的。

sentences.en: And so those people didn't have a script.
sentences.zh: 所以那些人没有剧本。

sentences.en: And in a very similar way, it seems like bullshit jobs put one in a similar situation.
sentences.zh: 以非常相似的方式，似乎狗屁工作让人处于类似的情况。

sentences.en: You don't know how you're supposed to feel about this.
sentences.zh: 你不知道你对这件事该有什么感觉。

sentences.en: You should be happy, but you're not.
sentences.zh: 你应该很高兴，但你并不高兴。

sentences.en: You don't know if you can talk about it.
sentences.zh: 你不知道自己是否能谈论这件事。

sentences.en: You don't know who you can confer.
sentences.zh: 你不知道该向谁咨询。

sentences.en: There's no kind of anchor to give yourself a sense of what's going on or what you should think or do about it.
sentences.zh: 你没有任何依靠，无法判断到底发生了什么，或者对此该想些什么、做些什么。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting ideas you explore is that in many countries, we have a fetish about work.
sentences.zh: 你探讨的最有趣的观点之一是，在许多国家，我们对工作有一种迷信。

sentences.en: We think a person who's working a job, even if it's a BS job, is in some ways a better human being than the person who's just hanging out.
sentences.zh: 我们认为一个有工作的人，哪怕是一份毫无意义的工作，在某种程度上也比一个无所事事的人更像个好人。

sentences.en: So it seems like there's a moral component to this whole belief structure.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种信仰结构似乎包含着一种道德成分。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I think this cannot be understood except through looking at the history of, well, for one thing, religion.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果不去审视历史，尤其是宗教的历史，就无法理解这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, if you look at the story of the Garden of Eden or even Hesiod's story of Prometheus, they both have the same basic theme, which is that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你看看伊甸园的故事，甚至是赫西俄德笔下普罗米修斯的故事，它们都有一个基本主题，那就是，你知道的，

sentences.en: we have to work because we disobeyed the gods or we disobeyed God.
sentences.zh: 我们必须工作，因为我们违抗了神，或者说违抗了上帝。

sentences.en: We rebelled and we were punished and gods are seen as creators.
sentences.zh: 我们反叛了，受到了惩罚，而神被视为创造者。

sentences.en: So in a way, we are punished.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们是在受罚。

sentences.en: They said, you want to be like God?
sentences.zh: 他们说，你想变得像上帝一样？

sentences.en: Fine, be like God.
sentences.zh: 好啊，那就变得像上帝一样吧。

sentences.en: You can create the world, but it'll be painful and miserable.
sentences.zh: 你可以创造世界，但过程会痛苦而悲惨。

sentences.en: So there's this notion that, A, work is productive and, B, that it is suffering and that it's kind of our punishment for our own arrogance.
sentences.zh: 所以有这样一种观念：第一，工作是生产性的；第二，工作是一种苦难，是我们因傲慢而受到的惩罚。

sentences.en: But at the same time, it's seen as moralizing.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它又被视为一种道德教化。

sentences.en: You know, through working, we become an adult, become a real, mature, self-contained, like, human being as opposed to kids who are just all over the place, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，通过工作，我们成为了成年人，成为了真正、成熟、独立的人，而不是像孩子那样随心所欲，对吧？

sentences.en: You know, through work, you become an adult.
sentences.zh: 你知道，通过工作，你才成为一个成年人。

sentences.en: So all of these ideas, work is production, work is punishment, work is necessary to retain maturity, all kind of bundled together.
sentences.zh: 所以所有这些观念——工作是生产、工作是惩罚、工作是保持成熟的必要条件——全都捆绑在了一起。

sentences.en: And what's happened is that there is this idea now that if you're not doing something, something you don't really enjoy,
sentences.zh: 现在发生的情况是，人们产生了一种观念：如果你没有在做某事，而且是你不怎么喜欢的事，

sentences.en: you're not working harder at it than you really want to be working, preferably for someone you don't like very much, well, you know, you're just a bad person.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有拼命地去做，最好还是为你不太喜欢的人工作，那么，你知道的，你就是一个糟糕的人。

sentences.en: You're not a real adult, certainly, and you're probably just some lazy parasite who doesn't deserve the help or support of their community.
sentences.zh: 你肯定不是一个真正的成年人，而且你可能只是个懒惰的寄生虫，不配得到社区的帮助或支持。

sentences.en: And that idea has been just drilled into people, like, incessantly for the last 30, 40 years.
sentences.zh: 这种观念在过去三四十年里被不断地灌输给人们。

sentences.en: Isn't it possible that there are actually jobs that people might find meaningless or pointless but that are, in fact, useful or essential?
sentences.zh: 有没有可能，有些工作人们觉得毫无意义或毫无价值，但实际上却是有用或必不可少的呢？

sentences.en: I mean, to take your example, it does seem absurd to ask Kurt to drive, you know, 100 miles to help move a computer 15 feet.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就拿你的例子来说，让库尔特开车跑100英里去帮忙挪动一台电脑15英尺，这确实显得很荒谬。

sentences.en: But maybe they have found, I'm just tossing this out, when you factor in liability or regulations or some other set of rules, that this is indeed the cheapest way to do something.
sentences.zh: 但也许他们发现——我只是随口一说——当你考虑到责任、法规或其他一系列规则时，这确实是完成某件事最便宜的方式。

sentences.en: So isn't it possible that at least in some cases, bullshit jobs have a purpose that might be invisible to the person who's working the job?
sentences.zh: 所以，有没有可能至少在某些情况下，狗屁工作有着某种目的，而这种目的对于从事该工作的人来说是不可见的？

sentences.en: Well, it's possible.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是有可能的。

sentences.en: And no doubt there are a few cases like that.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，确实有少数这样的例子。

sentences.en: But I think that the number of cases like that must be far outnumbered by the number of cases where it's the other way around.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这类情况的数量一定远少于相反的情况。

sentences.en: Because, after all, if there is some way that Kurt's job is really necessary, it seems unlikely that no one's going to explain that to him.
sentences.zh: 因为毕竟，如果库尔特的工作确实有某种必要性，那么没人向他解释这一点似乎不太可能。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you know, if you are working for a magazine that, it turns out, doesn't really exiSt.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你知道，如果你在一家实际上并不存在的杂志社工作……

sentences.en: I had an example like that.
sentences.zh: 我就遇到过这样的例子。

sentences.en: A magazine that doesn't exist?
sentences.zh: 一家不存在的杂志社？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She was writing for a travel magazine, you know, one of those ones they have in airplanes.
sentences.zh: 她当时在为一本旅游杂志写稿，你知道，就是飞机上那种杂志。

sentences.en: And gradually she figured out that it's a scam, you know.
sentences.zh: 后来她逐渐发现那是个骗局，你知道的。

sentences.en: Actually, there is no such magazine.
sentences.zh: 实际上，根本没有这本杂志。

sentences.en: They have this whole office full of people preparing copy and illustrations for a magazine that never is actually printed.
sentences.zh: 他们有一个办公室，里面坐满了人，在为一本永远不会印刷的杂志准备文案和插图。

sentences.en: Wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，等等。

sentences.en: Why were they doing that?
sentences.zh: 他们为什么要那样做？

sentences.en: She wasn't quite sure.
sentences.zh: 她也不太确定。

sentences.en: She thought it might have to do with a tax write-off or they got a grant or some sort of like, you know, there's some financial scam going on.
sentences.zh: 她认为这可能与抵税有关，或者他们拿到了补助金，或者就是某种金融诈骗。

sentences.en: There's lots of things like that going on.
sentences.zh: 这种事情多得很。

sentences.en: So if you're involved in a scam or something like that, you know, of course, that's the very thing they won't tell you.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你卷入了一场骗局或类似的事情，你知道，当然，那正是他们绝不会告诉你的事情。

sentences.en: So, you know, if there's a way that your job seems pointless but it's useful, chances are someone is going to explain that to you just because, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，如果你的工作看起来毫无意义但实际上有用，很可能有人会向你解释，因为，你知道，

sentences.en: you want your workers to be motivated.
sentences.zh: 你希望你的员工有动力。

sentences.en: On the other hand, you know, if you're writing reports for a central office and, you know, the central office just takes the reports and files them and never reads them,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，你知道，如果你在为总部写报告，而总部只是把报告收走存档，从来不读，

sentences.en: probably they're not going to tell you that.
sentences.zh: 他们大概是不会告诉你的。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the idea that jobs in some ways are jobs.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈关于工作在某些方面就是工作这一观点。

sentences.en: You know, they pay the bills, they cover the mortgage, they allow us to go on vacations.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们能支付账单，能还房贷，能让我们去度假。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the movie Dinner with Schmucks where the lead character explains to his girlfriend why he works at a job that he doesn't love.
sentences.zh: 我想给你放一段电影《笨人晚宴》的片段，主角向他的女朋友解释为什么他要从事一份他并不热爱的工作。

sentences.en: There's you and the me that you know, and we love each other, and we have a wonderful life.
sentences.zh: 有你认识的那个我，我们彼此相爱，生活得非常幸福。

sentences.en: But then there's the me that you don't know,
sentences.zh: 但还有你所不认识的那个我，

sentences.en: and the me that you don't know has to do things sometimes so that you and the me that you know can live in this nice apartment and eat at nice restaurants and go to Cabo for Christmas.
sentences.zh: 那个你所不认识的我，有时必须做些事情，这样你和那个你认识的我才能住在这间漂亮的公寓里，在高级餐厅用餐，圣诞节去卡波度假。

sentences.en: He takes care of us.
sentences.zh: 他在照顾我们。

sentences.en: You know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: There should not be any you I don't know.
sentences.zh: 不应该有任何你所不认识的我。

sentences.en: But there is.
sentences.zh: 但确实存在。

sentences.en: You might not like him.
sentences.zh: 你可能不会喜欢他。

sentences.en: I don't like him.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢他。

sentences.en: I hate him.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌他。

sentences.en: But we need him.
sentences.zh: 但我们需要他。

sentences.en: What do you think, David?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，大卫？

sentences.en: If we didn't have BS jobs, how would millions of people get paid?
sentences.zh: 如果我们没有狗屁工作，数以百万计的人该如何获得报酬？

sentences.en: Well, there's a lot of ways you could solve that problem.
sentences.zh: 嗯，解决这个问题的方法有很多。

sentences.en: Probably the easiest one would be just pay everybody and then let them sort out what they do for themselves.
sentences.zh: 最简单的方法可能就是直接付钱给每个人，然后让他们自己决定做什么。

sentences.en: Because we have this idea that's drilled into our heads that people want something for nothing.
sentences.zh: 因为我们脑子里被灌输了一种观念，认为人们想不劳而获。

sentences.en: But as I say, the very fact that people who are actually paid to do nothing are so unhappy shows that that's not really true.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，那些真正领着薪水却无所事事的人是如此不快乐，这恰恰证明了那并不是真的。

sentences.en: People really do want to have an effect on the world around them.
sentences.zh: 人们确实希望对周围的世界产生影响。

sentences.en: I always give the example of prisons.
sentences.zh: 我总是举监狱的例子。

sentences.en: Obviously, in America, you know, they basically force people to work.
sentences.zh: 显然，在美国，你知道，他们基本上是强迫人们工作。

sentences.en: But even where they don't, you know, where they have really nice prisons, they use withdrawing your work privileges as a way of punishing you.
sentences.zh: 但即使在没有强迫的地方，你知道，在那些条件很好的监狱里，他们也会把剥夺工作权利作为惩罚你的手段。

sentences.en: That is to say, you know, given a choice between sitting around playing cards or watching TV all day and pressing shorts in the prison laundry room, you know,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你知道，在整天坐着打牌、看电视和在监狱洗衣房里熨短裤之间做选择时，你知道，

sentences.en: even these mostly rather antisocial people, you know, would actually rather work than just sit around.
sentences.zh: 即使是这些大多相当反社会的人，你知道，实际上也宁愿工作而不愿闲坐着。

sentences.en: So people want to work.
sentences.zh: 所以人们是想工作的。

sentences.en: So I kind of support universal basic income.
sentences.zh: 所以我某种程度上支持全民基本收入。

sentences.en: I've kind of come around to the position that that's probably the best solution.
sentences.zh: 我已经倾向于认为这可能是最好的解决方案。

sentences.en: If we just give people, you know, we say, like, okay, all this technology, all these robots, you know, it's produced collectively by all of us.
sentences.zh: 如果我们只是给人们，你知道，我们说，好吧，所有这些技术，所有这些机器人，你知道，都是我们所有人共同创造的。

sentences.en: It's not like one person came up with that.
sentences.zh: 并不是某一个人想出来的。

sentences.en: That's a product of, you know, us and our ancestors doing hundreds of years of thinking and laboring.
sentences.zh: 那是我们和我们的祖先经过几百年的思考和劳动所创造的产物。

sentences.en: So let's pay us all back for that work, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以让我们为那份工作回报我们所有人，你知道。

sentences.en: Let's give everybody a basic income and leave it up to you to decide what to do.
sentences.zh: 让我们给每个人一份基本收入，然后由你自己决定做什么。

sentences.en: To be sure, a universal basic income is a controversial idea.
sentences.zh: 当然，全民基本收入是一个有争议的想法。

sentences.en: Also, while it would take care of essential needs, a basic income wouldn't buy people lots of dinners in fine restaurants or vacations in Cabo.
sentences.zh: 此外，虽然它能满足基本需求，但基本收入无法让人们在高档餐厅享用大餐或去卡波度假。

sentences.en: David's underlying point, though, is that instead of aspiring for greater material wealth, we should all seek more leisure time.
sentences.zh: 不过，大卫的核心观点是，我们不应该追求更多的物质财富，而应该追求更多的闲暇时间。

sentences.en: I know perfectly well that there's lots of societies, most societies, where people work distinctly less than they do today.
sentences.zh: 我非常清楚，有很多社会，大多数社会，人们的工作时间明显少于今天。

sentences.en: You know, probably the average oppressed medieval serf worked about half of what we work.
sentences.zh: 你知道，可能中世纪受压迫的农奴平均工作时间只有我们的一半。

sentences.en: But certainly people in other societies can be found to work two or three hours a day maximum.
sentences.zh: 但可以肯定的是，在其他社会中，人们每天最多工作两到三个小时。

sentences.en: So what do they do?
sentences.zh: 那么他们做什么呢？

sentences.en: They come up with incredibly interesting things to do.
sentences.zh: 他们会想出极其有趣的事情来做。

sentences.en: You know, we'd all be sitting around in cafes gossiping, and the gossip would get really interesting, you know, because people would have enough time to have lives.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们都会坐在咖啡馆里闲聊，而闲聊的内容会变得非常有趣，你知道，因为人们有足够的时间去生活。

sentences.en: We just don't know what it's like to actually have a life anymore, a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 我们很多人已经不知道真正拥有生活是什么感觉了。

sentences.en: If I didn't have to work and I still had money coming in,
sentences.zh: 如果我不必工作，而且还有收入来源，

sentences.en: I would be in a developing country in Africa helping people learn and participate in the democratic process and get rid of leaders who don't support their interests.
sentences.zh: 我会去非洲的发展中国家，帮助人们学习并参与民主进程，摆脱那些不支持他们利益的领导人。

sentences.en: I'd love to be in, like, a cover band.
sentences.zh: 我很想加入一个翻唱乐队。

sentences.en: I think that would be a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那会很有趣。

sentences.en: You know, Led Zeppelin, Black Sabbath, you know, those kind of genres.

sentences.en: If I didn't have to work, I'd go to Asia.
sentences.zh: 如果我不必工作，我会去亚洲。

sentences.en: You know, I would ensure that those individuals that have substance use disorder were really taken care of on an equitable level.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我会确保那些有药物滥用障碍的人在公平的层面上得到真正的照顾。

sentences.en: I mean, I like to go to space.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想去太空。

sentences.en: To space?
sentences.zh: 去太空？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If I have money and if I can do anything, I'd love to see the planet from up there.
sentences.zh: 如果我有钱，如果我能做任何事，我很想从上面看看这个星球。

sentences.en: David Graber is a professor of anthropology at the London School of Economics.
sentences.zh: 大卫·格雷伯是伦敦政治经济学院的人类学教授。

sentences.en: He studies theories of value and social constructs.
sentences.zh: 他研究价值理论和社会建构。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book, Bullshit Jobs.
sentences.zh: 他是《狗屁工作》一书的作者。

sentences.en: David, thanks for joining me today on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 大卫，感谢你今天参加《Hidden Brain》节目。
